title: Surface Area and Volume of 3D Objects
summary: Calculate the surface area and volume of cubes, rectangular prisms and triangular prisms, use nets, and convert between units of volume and capacity.

notes.text: A **prism** is a 3D object with two identical, parallel faces (the **bases**) joined by rectangular faces. The prism is named after the shape of its base: a **rectangular prism** has rectangular bases, a **triangular prism** has triangular bases, and a **cube** is a rectangular prism with all edges equal.

notes.caption: A rectangular prism (7 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm) and a triangular prism. Dashed lines are hidden edges.

notes.text: The **surface area** of a 3D object is the total area of all its faces. If you unfold the object flat, you get its **net**; the surface area is the area of the net. Units: $\text{cm}^2$, $\text{m}^2$.

notes.caption: Surface area formulae
rows: $2 \times \text{area of triangle} + \text{area of the three rectangles}$

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Calculate the surface area of the rectangular prism in the diagram ($l = 7$ cm, $b = 4$ cm, $h = 5$ cm).
steps: There are three pairs of equal faces.
Top and bottom: $2 \times 7 \times 4 = 56$; front and back: $2 \times 7 \times 5 = 70$; two ends: $2 \times 4 \times 5 = 40$.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a triangular prism
notes.problem: A triangular prism has right-angled triangles with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm as its ends. The prism is 10 cm long. Calculate its surface area.
steps: Three rectangles, one for each side of the triangle: $3 \times 10 + 4 \times 10 + 5 \times 10 = 120\ \text{cm}^2$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: In a triangular prism, the three rectangles are usually **different** sizes, because the triangle's sides are different. Each rectangle has the length of the prism and the width of one side of the triangle.
**Volume** is the amount of space a 3D object takes up. It is measured in **cubic units**: $\text{mm}^3$, $\text{cm}^3$, $\text{m}^3$.

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem:
(a) Find the volume of the rectangular prism in the diagram.
(b) A triangular prism has a triangle with base 6 cm and height 4 cm, and is 10 cm long. Find its volume.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Two different "heights" appear in a triangular prism: the height of the **triangle** (used for its area) and the length (or height) of the **prism**. Label your sketch so you do not mix them up.
**Capacity** is the amount a container can hold, usually measured in millilitres (ml), litres (l) and kilolitres (kl). Volume and capacity are linked:

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Volume conversions use the **cube** of the length conversion. $1\ \text{m} = 100\ \text{cm}$, so $1\ \text{m}^3 = 100 \times 100 \times 100 = 1\ 000\ 000\ \text{cm}^3$, not $100\ \text{cm}^3$.

notes.title: Worked example 4: a water tank
notes.problem: A rectangular water tank is 2 m long, 1,5 m wide and 1 m high. How many litres of water can it hold?

notes.text: If every edge of a cube is doubled, the surface area is multiplied by $2^2 = 4$ and the volume is multiplied by $2^3 = 8$. A cube with edge 2 cm has volume $8\ \text{cm}^3$; a cube with edge 4 cm has volume $64\ \text{cm}^3$, which is 8 times as big.

items: Surface area = total area of all faces (the net). Cube: $6s^2$; rectangular prism: $2(lb + lh + bh)$.
Volume of a prism = area of base × height. Cube: $s^3$; rectangular prism: $lbh$.
Triangular prism: volume $= \frac{1}{2}bh \times$ length; surface area = 2 triangles + 3 rectangles.
Doubling every edge multiplies surface area by 4 and volume by 8.

options: Sum of the areas of all faces
questions.explanation: Volume of a prism = area of the base × the height (length) of the prism.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base 6 cm and height 4 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. Calculate its volume.
Match each volume with the equal capacity.
How many cubes with 2 cm edges fit exactly into a box measuring 10 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm?
questions.explanation: $5$ along the length, $3$ across and $2$ up: $5 \times 3 \times 2 = 30$. (Or $240 \div 8 = 30$.)

questions.prompt: A rectangular prism has a volume of $120\ \text{cm}^3$. Its base is 6 cm by 5 cm. Calculate its height.
How many squares does the net of a cube have?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares.

Volume is multiplied by 8 ✓ (1)
